definitions.gloss: objective viewpoint; viewing something objectively; seeing from a detached perspective
definitions.explanation: The act of looking at something — especially oneself or one's own situation — from an impartial, detached standpoint rather than a subjective or emotional one.

examples.japanese: {自分|じぶん}を{客観視|きゃっかんし}する。
{状況|じょうきょう}を{客観視|きゃっかんし}して{冷静|れいせい}に{判断|はんだん}する{必要|ひつよう}がある。
examples.english: You need to view the situation objectively and make calm judgments.

examples.japanese: {失敗|しっぱい}した{時|とき}こそ{感情的|かんじょうてき}にならず、{自分|じぶん}の{行動|こうどう}を{客観視|きゃっかんし}することが{成長|せいちょう}につながる。
examples.english: It is precisely when you fail that viewing your own actions objectively — rather than getting emotional — leads to growth.

notes:
A compound of {客観|きゃっかん} (objectivity) and {視|し} (viewing/seeing). Functions as a suru-verb: {客観視|きゃっかんし}する means "to view objectively."

This word is commonly used in self-improvement, business, psychology, and counseling contexts. The ability to {自分|じぶん}を{客観視|きゃっかんし}する (see oneself objectively) is considered an important skill in Japanese professional culture, often discussed in job interviews and performance reviews.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {自分|じぶん}を{客観視|きゃっかんし}する: to view oneself objectively
- {状況|じょうきょう}を{客観視|きゃっかんし}する: to view the situation objectively
- {客観視|きゃっかんし}できる: to be able to see objectively
- {客観視|きゃっかんし}が{難|むずか}しい: difficult to view objectively

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {客観的|きゃっかんてき}: objective (adjective)
- {俯瞰|ふかん}: bird's-eye view (looking at the big picture)
- {主観|しゅかん}: subjectivity (the opposite perspective)
